class py4radiation.HeatingCoolingTables(run_dir, run_name, loop_columns=None)

Bases: object

Process and format heating and cooling tables for HD/MHD codes.

This class reads the outputs of pyCIAO to generate a single table containing hydrogen number density, temperature, heating and cooling rates and mean molecular weight.

Attributes:
run_dirPath

Directory containing the pyCIAO run file and data maps.

run_namestr

The common identifier (stem) of the pyCIAO run.

DEFAULT_LOOP_COLUMNS: tuple[LoopColumn, ...] = (LoopColumn(command='hden', output_header='HDEN[cm^-3]', input_scale='log10', factor=1.0),)
write_table(outdir='.', outfile=None)

Write the heating/cooling rates table.

Parameters:
outdirstr or Path, optional

Directory where the table will be saved. Defaults to ‘.’ (current directory).

outfilestr, optional

Name of the output file. If None, defaults to ‘{run_name}_cooltable.dat’. This file is saved in the current directory.

Returns:
Path

The full path to the generated table.

class py4radiation.IonTables(run_dir, run_name, elements)

Bases: object

A class to generate ion fraction tables from pyCIAO/Cloudy output files.

This class parses a simulation run configuration, loads distributed ion fraction maps, and generates a single HDF5 file suitable for astrophysical codes.

Attributes:
run_dirPath

Directory containing the pyCIAO run file and data maps.

run_namestr

The common identifier of the pyCIAO run.

write_table()

Write the ion fractions table.

class py4radiation.SED(run_name, custom_table=False, table_id='fig2a', table=None, distance_kpc=1, age_myr=3)

Bases: object

A class to load, process and format SEDs for pyCIAO.

This class handles the conversion of Leitherer et al. (1999) style SED tables into pyCIAO/Cloudy-readable formats.

For scaling, consider an object of interest located at a user-specified distance from the radiation source.

Attributes:
run_namestr

Name of the run, used for output filenames.

distance_cmfloat

Distance of the object of interest to the source in cm.

data_tablenp.NDArray[np.float64]

Raw loaded SED data table.

redshiftfloat

Redshift (z) of the source. For this version, only consider the near Universe (z=0.0000e+00).

get_sed()

Calculates Energy (Ryd) and Specific flux (F_nu).

Returns:
